note: No possession of a wireless device on person during the instructional day (must be off and stored). Feb 2024 SBE resolution only encouraged district limits.

policy_type: requires districts to adopt a policy
note: Districts must adopt a policy regulating possession/use during school hours incl. lunch and passing; no ban mandated. Preceded by State Board of Education directive 2024-10-11. Not counted by EdWeek as requiring a ban.

policy_type: requires districts to adopt a policy
note: Districts must adopt policies that 'limit' wireless device use during the school day and restrict social-media access on school internet. EdWeek classifies as bell-to-bell; Ballotpedia as 'limits use in classrooms'.

law_or_rule_citation: SB 142 (Bell to Bell, No Cell Act, 2025)
note: District policies (approved by DESE) must restrict possession and prohibit use during the school day. 2024 pilot grant for pouches (2024-07-02).

policy_type: requires districts to adopt a policy
note: Districts, county offices and charters must adopt (by 2026-07-01, update every 5 years) a policy to limit or prohibit smartphone use at school; may be a full ban. AB 272 (2019) had merely permitted limits.

policy_type: requires districts to adopt a policy
note: Policy on possession/use during the school day required by 2026-07-01; content left to districts.

policy_type: requires districts to adopt a policy
note: 2025 law requires every district to adopt a smartphone policy by 2026-27 using CSDE guidance (Public Act number and signing date not verified). Aug 2026 SBE guidance 'strongly recommends' bell-to-bell; a statutory bell-to-bell ban failed in the 2026 session. Ballotpedia lists only the 2024 guidance.

policy_type: requires districts to adopt a policy
note: Districts/charters must adopt a policy that at minimum limits use during instructional time. Effective year assumed (not verified). $250k pouch pilot in 2024.

law_or_rule_citation: DCPS Student Cell Phone and Electronic Device Policy (announced 2025-06-06); DC Council Distraction-Free Learning Amendment Act of 2025 (passed 2025-07-01)
note: DCPS bell-to-bell from 2025-26 (all grades); Council act extends to charters, full effect 2026-27 (council act details from press coverage, not the enrolled act).

grades_covered: K-8 bell-to-bell (from 2025-26); 9-12 instructional time (6-district full-day pilot 2025-26)
note: First state law: HB 379 banned use during instructional time from 2023-24 and required social-media blocks on school Wi-Fi. HB 1105 (signed 2025-05-30) made K-8 phone-free for the whole school day from 2025-26 and created a 6-district high-school full-day pilot (report due 2026-12-01). Orange County district bell-to-bell from Aug 2023.
HB 340 signed 2025-05-09 (K-8, effective 2026-07-01); HB 1009 signed 2026-05-05 extends to high school from 2027-07-01.
Single statewide district; policy, not statute. Ballotpedia table gives 2026-02-02, timeline 2026-02-12.

policy_type: requires districts to adopt a policy
note: SB 1032 requires each district/charter to adopt a 'distraction-free learning' policy minimizing device use by 2025-12-31; no ban mandated (signing day not verified). EO offered $5,000 to districts adopting policies. EdWeek counts Idaho as bell-to-bell; Ballotpedia lists only the EO.

grades_covered: K-12 (districts may allow HS use at lunch/passing)
note: School boards must adopt policies prohibiting use during school time by start of 2027-28.
Prohibits wireless devices (phones, tablets, laptops) during instructional time; teacher/emergency exceptions.
District policies must restrict use during classroom instructional time (from 2025-07-01). Ballotpedia labels it a statewide ban.
Devices off and stored away during the school day. Dec 2024 SBE task-force recommendation was non-binding.
District policies must prohibit use during the school day with exceptions; social media blocked on school tech.
No possession on person throughout the instructional day; devices off and stowed.
LD 1234 (2025-06-09) only required a policy; LD 2212 requires bell-to-bell prohibition by 2026-08-01.
County boards must implement bell-to-bell policies by 2027-28; no suspension/expulsion solely for violations. Montgomery County adopts bell-to-bell district-wide in 2026-27.
Both chambers passed bell-to-bell bills but versions were not reconciled/signed as of Aug 2026. No state mandate.
Districts must implement policy prohibiting use on school grounds during instructional time.

policy_type: requires districts to adopt a policy
note: Districts/charters must adopt a cellphone policy by 2025-03-15; content unspecified. A K-8 bell-to-bell / 9-12 classroom ban bill was pending in the 2026 session (outcome not verified; Ballotpedia July 2026 lists only SF 3567).

law_or_rule_citation: SB 2151 (2025) passed Senate, died; HB 570 (2026) died
note: No statewide action.
Policies must prohibit display/use from start to end of school day incl. meals, breaks, passing. Ballotpedia table gives 2025-07-07, timeline 2025-07-09.
Letter asking districts to consider 'cell phone-free' policies; no statute.
Policies must prohibit use on school property or at school functions, with exceptions.

District policies must prohibit access during class (exceptions). Ballotpedia counts NV among bell-to-bell states; statute text targets class time. Clark County used signal-blocking pouches for grades 6-12 from 2024-25.
Policies must prohibit all personal device use from first bell to dismissal bell.
Boards adopt policies per NJDOE guidelines prohibiting non-academic use on school grounds during the school day; NJDOE updated guidelines Jan 2026.

policy_type: requires districts to adopt a policy
note: Districts/charters must adopt a wireless-device policy per PED guidelines; no ban mandated.

law_or_rule_citation: FY2026 state budget (S3006-C, Education Article VII), enacted 2025-05-09
note: Districts/charters must prohibit use during the school day (bell-to-bell) from 2025-26; ~$13.5M for storage. NYC DOE had banned phones until 2015-03-02 (ban lifted under de Blasio).
Policies (submitted by 2026-01-01) must prohibit using, displaying or having a device on during instructional time; districts may go bell-to-bell. EdWeek counts NC as bell-to-bell.
Devices (incl. smartwatches) stored and inaccessible during the school day; districts must collect data on mental health, attendance and achievement effects.
HB 250 (2024-05-20) required district policies limiting use (2024-25). HB 96 requires policies prohibiting all use during the instructional day, adopted by 2026-01-01.
SB 139 mandated bell-to-bell for 2025-26 only (optional thereafter); HB 1276 (spring 2026, signing date not verified) made the prohibition permanent.
Districts required to adopt policies by 2025-10-31 and implement by 2026-01-01 prohibiting devices during regular instructional hours (bell-to-bell). Oct 2024 ODE guidance was a recommendation.

law_or_rule_citation: Act 2024 (School Safety grant amendment, $100M for pouches, 2024-07-11); HB passed House 2026-06-01
note: Grant funding only; a bill requiring district restrictions passed the House June 2026 but not the Senate as of Aug 2026. Philadelphia leaves policy to schools.
Policies must prohibit physical access to devices during the school day; effective 2026-08-01.

law_or_rule_citation: FY2024-25 Appropriations Act proviso 1.103; SBE model policy
note: Districts must implement SBE model policy prohibiting access during the school day to receive State Aid to Classrooms; in force from January 2025. Re-enacted in later budgets.
Governor Rhoden opposed a statewide ban; no state action.
Policies must prohibit use during instructional time, with exceptions.
Districts/charters must prohibit use of personal communication devices on school property during the school day. Houston ISD implemented from Aug 2025.
SB 178 (2025-03-25) banned use during classroom hours from 2025-26 as a default LEAs could modify; SB 69 extends to the whole school day from 2026-27.

grades_covered: K-12 (public and publicly funded independent schools)
note: Arrival-to-dismissal prohibition per Secretary of Education policy; also restricts school social-media use.

EO 33 directed VDOE guidance (final Sept 2024, in force 2025-01-01). 2025 law codified bell-to-bell from 2025-26; SB 108 (2026-04-06) extends to possession/use anywhere on school property bell to bell from 2026-27.

law_or_rule_citation: OSPI superintendent guidance 2024-09-06; SSB 5346 (2026) OSPI study
note: Superintendent Reykdal 'challenged' districts to restrict in-class use by 2025-26; 2026 law only directs OSPI to collect policies and report by 2027-12-15. Governor Ferguson plans a bell-to-bell bill for the 2027 session.
Devices inaccessible during instructional time; boards may go further.
Policies prohibiting use during instructional time required by 2026-07-01.

policy_type: requires districts to adopt a policy
note: Every district board must adopt a policy on possession/use; no ban required.
